title: Signs forgotten
summary: The people forget the signs and wonders they had heard, grow hard-hearted and disbelieving, and imagine that the signs were wrought by men and the devil.

explicit_facts.text: The people began to forget the signs and wonders they had heard and became hard in their hearts and blind in their minds.
They imagined the signs were wrought by men and by the power of the devil, and regarded Christ's doctrine as foolish and vain.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People gathered in an unspecified community setting; their expressions may suggest disbelief.

narration.text: the people began to forget those signs and wonders

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The spiritual decline is narrated; no supernatural appearance is described.

title: Wickedness grows
summary: The people grow in wickedness and abominations, disbelieve that more signs will be given, and are led and tempted by Satan.

explicit_facts.text: The people grew strong in wickedness and abominations and did not believe more signs or wonders would be given.
Satan went about leading and tempting the people and causing them to do great wickedness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Show a community in a general state of moral decline without depicting a specific unstated act.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Satan's activity is reported; the verse does not describe a visible appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not give Satan a visible form or depict a specific unstated sin.

title: Years counted
summary: The ninety-sixth through ninety-ninth years pass. The account notes one hundred years since Mosiah's days, six hundred and nine years since Lehi left Jerusalem, and nine years since the sign of Christ's coming; the Nephites reckon time from that sign.

explicit_facts.text: The ninety-sixth, ninety-seventh, ninety-eighth, and ninety-ninth years passed.
One hundred years had passed since Mosiah's days as king over the Nephites.
Six hundred and nine years had passed since Lehi left Jerusalem.
Nine years had passed since the sign spoken of by the prophets that Christ should come into the world.
The Nephites began reckoning time from the sign or the coming of Christ.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A nonliteral calendar or passage-of-time graphic may convey the chronology.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are chronological statements, not separate historical scenes.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage Lehi's departure, Mosiah's reign, or Christ's coming as present events.

title: Nephi does not return
summary: Nephi, the father of Nephi who had charge of the records, did not return to Zarahemla and could nowhere be found in the land.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi, father of the Nephi who had charge of the records, did not return to Zarahemla and could nowhere be found in the land.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse does not say where Nephi went.

title: The people take up arms
summary: In the thirteenth year, the Gadianton robbers' killings and destruction prompt Nephites and Lamanites, including converted Lamanites, to take up arms against them.

explicit_facts.text: In the thirteenth year, wars and contentions began throughout the land; the Gadianton robbers had become numerous, slain many people, and laid waste many cities.
The Nephites and Lamanites took up arms against the robbers.
Lamanites converted unto the Lord united with their Nephite brethren and took up arms for their families, rights, worship, freedom, and liberty.
